# ADR-0007: SLOs from span metrics, rules generated by Sloth

Status: Accepted

## Context

Multi-window multi-burn-rate alerts are easy to get subtly wrong by hand. We also want the SLI to come from the same data an engineer sees on the dashboards.

## Decision

- SLIs come from `storefront` SERVER spans via the collector's span metrics (`docs/slo.md` lists the frozen metric names).
- SLOs are declared in `slo/storefront.yml` (Sloth `prometheus/v1`): availability 99.5% and latency 99% under 300 ms, both over 30 days.
- `make slo` runs Sloth in a container and writes `prometheus/rules/slo/storefront.generated.yml`. The generated file is committed. CI regenerates it and fails on any diff.
- Sloth runs at build time only. Prometheus loads plain rule files, tested with `promtool test rules` (`tests/prometheus/slo_test.yml`).
- Alert names: `StorefrontAvailabilityBurn` and `StorefrontLatencyBurn`, with `severity=page` and `severity=ticket` variants and a `runbook_url` on each.
- Prometheus has no lifecycle API enabled here, so a rule file added after start is not seen until Prometheus is restarted.

## Consequences

- The window math is not ours to maintain.
- Changing an objective means editing the spec and regenerating, not editing the generated file.
- The 30-day window means a fresh stack has no history. The burn-rate alerts still work, because they use short windows.

## Alternatives considered

- Hand-written rules: fine for one SLO, error-prone for several.
- Pyrra: adds a runtime service that has to be run and secured.
